ai.definition: RAG pipelines for AI research combine retrieval-based and generative models to efficiently retrieve relevant information from large datasets and generate new insights or summaries.
ai.howItWorks: These pipelines first use a retrieval model to quickly find relevant documents or passages from vast knowledge bases. Then, a generative model processes this retrieved information to create new content, such as summaries, answers, or even entirely new text that builds on the existing data.
ai.problemSolved: Addressing the challenge of efficiently processing and utilizing large volumes of unstructured data in AI research by leveraging both retrieval and generation capabilities.
ai.buildProcess: Developed through iterative training of machine learning models, fine-tuning on specific datasets relevant to the research domain, and continuous optimization for performance and efficiency.
ai.costDrivers: Data collection and preprocessing costs, computational resources for model training, ongoing maintenance and updates, human oversight during development and testing phases.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: expected to transition into early commercialization as more applications are validated in real-world scenarios.
ai.regulation: Currently not subject to specific regulations but may be influenced by broader AI guidelines and data privacy laws.
ai.risks: Technical risks related to model accuracy, bias, and ethical considerations; economic risks due to high initial investment and uncertain market demand; regulatory risks as the technology matures and is applied more widely.
ai.profitability: Uncertain at this stage, dependent on successful commercialization and adoption by research institutions and enterprises.
ai.futureDevelopment: Potential for integration with other AI technologies like computer vision and natural language processing to expand application areas; development of more advanced models that can handle even larger datasets and more complex tasks.

glossary.def: A combination of retrieval and generative AI models used to process large volumes of unstructured data efficiently.
An AI model designed to quickly find relevant documents or passages from a knowledge base based on input queries.
An AI model capable of generating new content, such as summaries, answers, or entirely new text, based on the provided data.
